components.css: .ds-nav { font-family: 'Public Sans Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; width: 220px; background: #fff; border-right: 1px solid #e5e7eb; } .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border-left: 4px solid transparent; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; color: #4b5563; text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: #f9fafb; color: #111827; } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #fca5a5; } .ds-nav-active { border-left-color: #dc2626; background: #fef2f2; color: #b91c1c; font-weight: 600; } .ds-nav-active:hover { background: #fef2f2; color: #b91c1c; } .ds-nav-locked { color: #9ca3af; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-nav-locked:hover { background: transparent; color: #9ca3af; }

components.name: Record Card

components.css: .ds-table { font-family: 'Public Sans Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; width: 420px; border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 0; background: #fff; border: 1px solid #e5e7eb; text-align: left; } .ds-table th { height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; background: #f3f4f6; border-bottom: 1px solid #e5e7eb; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #6b7280; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-table td { height: 56px; padding: 0 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid #e5e7eb; font-size: 13px; color: #111827; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; max-width: 22rem; } .ds-table tbody tr:last-child td { border-bottom: 0; } .ds-table tbody tr:hover td { background: #f9fafb; } .ds-mono { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 12px; }

narrative.overview:
AKAY looks like a well-kept logbook at a health center: white sheets ruled with hairlines on a pale gray desk. Nothing floats, nothing is rounded for charm, and nothing is decorated. Structure comes from 1px borders and consistent row heights, so a midwife scanning forty rows at the end of a clinic day lands on the same column in the same place every time. Red is the single mark of attention. It appears on the one primary action, on the active place in navigation, and, in its alert form, when something is wrong or irreversible.

The register is dense but not cramped. Body text is 14px, headings are bold sans, and IDs and codes sit in monospace. Screens are built for repeated daily work on a desktop or laptop in a facility, sometimes over a weak connection, so loading and error states are first-class parts of the system rather than afterthoughts. The interface should feel competent and calm to someone on a long shift, and never promotional.

The system does not suggest, diagnose, or decorate. Clinical fields look like fields a trained person fills in. Saved records look permanent. Locked modules are visible and honest about being locked.
keyCharacteristics: Flat sheets separated by 1px hairlines; a visible shadow only on floating layers.
Square corners everywhere. A 2px radius on small tags is the only softening, and the pill shape is reserved for dots, avatars, and status chips.
One red. Primary actions and active states use it, and urgency uses its alert form. Ordinary state uses green, amber, and cyan.
Fixed-size tables: the same row height whether the page has three rows or ten.
Cool-gray neutrals tinted toward blue, never warm.

rules.name: The One Stamp Rule
rules.body: Red marks the one thing to do or the one thing that is wrong. Brand red is for action and place; Alert Red is for danger. If a screen has red everywhere, none of it is read.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Not-Danger Rule
rules.body: Ordinary state (completed, pending, low stock) uses green, amber, or cyan. Alert Red is never spent on state that is merely noteworthy.

rules.name: The Tokens-First Rule
rules.body: Screens reference role tokens (`--color-text`, `--color-surface`, `--color-primary`) or the neutral and brand ramps. Raw `slate-*` utilities and hardcoded hex such as `#0F172A`, `#F8FAFC`, or `#B91C1C` are drift from before the token rework and are migration targets, not part of the system.

rules.name: The Dense-But-Legible Rule
rules.body: Body is 14px, not 16px, because rows and records are the product. Do not go below 10px, and only labels may be that small.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Identity Rule
rules.body: If a value is something a person might read aloud or copy (an ID, a code), it is monospace.

rules.name: The Fixed-Frame Rule
rules.body: A table or list card holds its size regardless of row count. Empty and error states fill the same frame instead of collapsing it.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Sheets do not lift on hover. Hover changes a border to Rule Strong or a fill to Ledger Sheet Sunk; it never moves the element or adds a shadow. The existing `.card-hover` lift and the `SectionCard` hover translate and shadow are drift from this rule.

dos: Do build surfaces from Ledger Sheet on Ledger Paper with 1px Rule Hairline borders, adding only the card hairline shadow on top-level sheets.
Do use Register Red (#dc2626) for fills and Register Red Deep (#b91c1c) for red text, active states, and hover.
Do reserve Alert Red (#ef4444) for danger, urgency, errors, and destructive confirms.
Do use the green, amber, and cyan families for ordinary status.
Do keep table rows at 56px and headers at 44px, and truncate long text with an ellipsis and a title.
Do put IDs and codes in IBM Plex Mono.
Do reference `--color-*` role tokens or the neutral and brand ramps instead of raw hex.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`, and keep motion to short fades and state transitions.
Do show locked modules as visible, labeled placeholders.
donts: Don't round corners, other than the 2px badge radius and the pill on dots, avatars, and status chips.
Don't lift, translate, or add a shadow to a card on hover.
Don't introduce `slate-*` utilities or new hardcoded hex values; they are migration targets.
Don't use red for anything that is not an action, an active place, or a danger.
Don't blur real data to indicate a lock; render a placeholder.
Don't make type larger or looser for decoration; density is intentional.
Don't add features that read as clinical suggestions, such as auto-suggested diagnoses or recommended treatments.
